scope: Named, grafted persimmons for zone 6b: American persimmon (Diospyros virginiana) cultivars, American × Asian hybrids, and Asian (D. kaki) cultivars only when a seller rates them hardy to zone 6. Most Asian types (Fuyu, Jiro, Hachiya, Giombo, Tamopan and similar) are rated zone 7+ and are left out; so are ungrafted seedlings.

varieties.name: Nikita's Gift
varieties.summary: Cold-hardy American × Asian hybrid; sweet, reddish-orange fruit, hardy to about −10°F.
varieties.description: A Diospyros virginiana × kaki hybrid from the Nikita Botanical Garden in Yalta, Crimea, sold as Nikitskaya Bordovaya. Sweet, flavorful reddish-orange fruit eaten soft, on a compact self-fertile tree (10–12 ft) with orange-yellow fall color; sellers rate it hardy to about −10°F.

varieties.name: Rosseyanka
varieties.summary: Russian hybrid; large, nearly seedless golden fruit, zone 5 hardy.
varieties.description: A Russian D. virginiana × kaki hybrid from the Nikita Botanical Garden in Yalta. Large (2–3 in), nearly seedless golden-orange fruit that is sweet when soft and ripens late; England's Orchard reports trees surviving temperatures in the −20s °F.

varieties.name: JT-02 (Mikkusu)
varieties.summary: Josephine × Taishu hybrid; orange fruit that hangs into late November.
varieties.description: A hybrid from a cross of the American ‘Josephine’ and the Asian ‘Taishu’. Rich orange fruit ripening late October into November that can hang on the tree until Thanksgiving, on a compact tree.

varieties.name: Kasandra
varieties.summary: Great Wall × hybrid backcross by David Lavergne; brix 21, hardy to −11°F.
varieties.description: Hybridized by David Lavergne from ‘Great Wall’ crossed with an F2 male of a Rosseyanka hybrid backcrossed to American persimmon. 2.5–3 in fruit measuring 21 brix, mid-season; England's Orchard reports it cold-hardy to −11°F with no freeze damage (zones 5b–6).

varieties.name: Sosnovskaya
varieties.summary: Eastern European American × Asian hybrid.
varieties.description: An American × Asian hybrid of Eastern European origin offered by Future Forest Plants. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Chuchupaka
varieties.summary: Eastern European American × Asian hybrid.
varieties.description: An American × Asian hybrid of Eastern European origin offered by Future Forest Plants. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Journey
varieties.summary: American × Asian hybrid offered by Future Forest Plants.
varieties.description: An American × Asian hybrid persimmon offered by Future Forest Plants. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Zhima Khurma (NB-02)
varieties.summary: Hybrid selection NB-02; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A hybrid persimmon sold as NB-02 ‘Zhima Khurma’ by Future Forest Plants. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Saijo
varieties.summary: Small, very sweet Asian persimmon rated to zone 6.
varieties.description: A Japanese Diospyros kaki rated hardy to zone 6 by Edible Landscaping. Small, yellow-orange, conical fruit with an elegant sweet flavor when soft, few seeds and reliable annual crops; resists cracking.

varieties.name: Great Wall
varieties.summary: Chinese Asian persimmon that has survived −5°F winters in zone 6b.
varieties.description: A Chinese Diospyros kaki introduced to the U.S. by J. Russell Smith, rated zones 6–9 by several sellers. Medium, squarish, slightly flattened fruit eaten soft, red fall foliage, and a self-fertile, disease-resistant tree; a zone 6b grower reports it unharmed after −5°F winters.

varieties.name: Prok
varieties.summary: Very large, few-seeded American persimmon; ripens early.
varieties.description: An American persimmon with very large, few-seeded fruit ripening from August into October. England's Orchard credits it to the Cornell University breeding program, grown out by John Gordon of Amherst, NY.

varieties.name: Yates
varieties.summary: Large, early American persimmon; also sold as Juhl.
varieties.description: A large-fruited, early-ripening American persimmon, also sold as ‘Juhl’ or ‘Yates/Juhl’, and a parent of ‘Wonderful’.

varieties.summary: American persimmon sold for northern gardens.
varieties.description: An American persimmon widely sold for northern gardens. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.description: A long-established named American persimmon grown for early-ripening golden fruit.

varieties.description: A named American persimmon valued for large fruit. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.description: A named American persimmon sold by One Green World. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.description: A named American persimmon sold by One Green World. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Morse
varieties.summary: Late-dropping American persimmon selected by Morse Nursery.
varieties.description: A grafted American persimmon selection propagated by Morse Nursery (West Lafayette, IN) from its own mother trees. Heavy-cropping female cultivar with fruit dropping October–December, grown mainly for wildlife food plots.

varieties.name: September (A33)
varieties.summary: Early-dropping American persimmon selection (cultivar A33) from Morse Nursery.
varieties.description: A grafted American persimmon selection (cultivar designation A33) propagated by Morse Nursery. Female cultivar bred for heavy, consistent fruit drop throughout September.

varieties.name: August
varieties.summary: Early-dropping American persimmon selection from Morse Nursery.
varieties.description: A grafted American persimmon selection propagated by Morse Nursery, bred for an early fruit drop concentrated in August.

varieties.description: A numbered American persimmon selection offered by England's Orchard & Nursery. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Steiermark
varieties.summary: Austrian-named Asian persimmon; seller rates it hardy to warmer zone 6 with winter protection.
varieties.description: A Diospyros kaki persimmon named for Steiermark (Styria), an Austrian province in the southern Alps where the original tree was found; received by Cricket Hill Garden from Cliff England of Sand Gap, Kentucky. Astringent fruit; the seller rates it hardy to warmer areas of zone 6 with winter protection, no protection needed in zones 7-9.

varieties.name: Downingtown Center
varieties.summary: Late-summer American persimmon from John Hershey's Pennsylvania nursery.
varieties.description: A named American persimmon from John Hershey's farm in Downingtown, Pennsylvania, described by Future Forest Plants as one of the best there. Fruit ripens from late August into October. Possibly an old cultivar, Golden Gem, under a lost name.

varieties.name: Josephine
varieties.summary: Older Missouri American persimmon that drops its fruit all at once.
varieties.description: An older American persimmon from Bluffton, Missouri. Future Forest Plants notes it drops nearly all its fruit within about two weeks in September.

varieties.name: Korp
varieties.summary: Named American persimmon sold by Future Forest Plants.
varieties.description: A named American persimmon offered by Future Forest Plants, which gives no further description. Limited independent detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: McKenzie Middle
varieties.summary: Large, late American persimmon from John Hershey's farm.
varieties.description: A large-fruited American persimmon from John Hershey's farm, listed by Future Forest Plants as a seedling of Early Golden. Fruit ripens October to November.

varieties.name: NC-10
varieties.summary: Large, egg-shaped American persimmon selected in Ontario.
varieties.description: An American persimmon selection from R. Douglas Campbell of Ontario. Future Forest Plants describes the fruit as large, egg-shaped and dense with excellent flavor. The original tree's location is unknown.

varieties.name: Rich Tooie
varieties.summary: Tennessee American persimmon noted for flavor.
varieties.description: A 60-chromosome American persimmon from Tennessee, introduced by TN Hunter through the Growing Fruit forum. Future Forest Plants notes its outstanding flavor.

varieties.name: TY Gateway
varieties.summary: Wild Mississippi selection introduced by The Garden Farmacy.
varieties.description: A wild American persimmon from Ridgeland, Mississippi, introduced by Taylor Yowell of The Garden Farmacy nursery. Limited further detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Celebrity (U20A)
varieties.summary: American persimmon sold by Beautiful Beginnings Nursery.
varieties.description: A named American persimmon (U20A) offered by Beautiful Beginnings Nursery for USDA zones 5-9. The seller has not yet posted a full description.

varieties.name: Tin Cup
varieties.summary: Self-fruitful American persimmon from a ~30-year-old tree in northwestern New York.
varieties.description: A grafted, self-fruitful female American persimmon whose parent tree grows in northwestern New York. Blue Hill describes very sweet fruit that drops from early October into mid-November and ripens on the tree, on a very vigorous tree rated zones 5-9. The seller lists resistance to apple scab, cedar apple rust, fire blight and powdery mildew.
